lecture_title: Charged Particles, Field Transformations, and Relativistic Waves

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: Shows the momentum form of force while the electric term of the Lorentz law is being placed on the board.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: And then Lorentz discovered another term.
assets.caption_hint: Momentum form of the Lorentz force

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Preserves the provisional antisymmetric array while its three independent entries are identified with cross-product components.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The anti-symmetric tensor is one form of the cross product.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed cyclic component identities that determine the corrected sign pattern.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We can go back and forth between vector and anti-symmetric tensor.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: Shows the magnetic field in both vector and antisymmetric spatial-tensor form.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It can be represented either as a vector or an anti-symmetric tensor.
assets.caption_hint: Magnetic field as an antisymmetric tensor

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: Provides a clear board state for the third cross-product component and its contraction form.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That's another way of writing the Lorentz force law here.
assets.caption_hint: Magnetic cross product as a tensor contraction

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: Shows the paired terms whose cancellation proves that a pure magnetic force does not change speed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: If we multiply it on both of its indices by the same vector, we always get zero.
assets.caption_hint: Antisymmetric cancellation in the no-work proof

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Preserves the original three-axis sketch motivating electric-magnetic mixing; a clean redraw follows it in the notes.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: In order to get the equations really relativistically correct, we're going to have to work with four vectors.
assets.caption_hint: Laboratory and co-moving descriptions of the force

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: Shows the magnetic block and electric time-space entries being assembled into the field tensor.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Anti-symmetric tensor, six independent components, constituting the electromagnetic field tensor.
assets.caption_hint: Construction of the electromagnetic field tensor

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: Shows four-velocity, gamma, and four-momentum together at the completed board state.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The momentum is M times u mu.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: Shows the unit norm of four-velocity and the derivative leading to four-force orthogonality.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It follows that f mu times u sub mu must equal zero.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: Shows the covariant force ansatz and its vanishing contraction on the same board.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Let's first look at it for slow velocities.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Shows the ordinary Lorentz force recovered after converting the proper-time derivative to coordinate time.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: So it looks exactly like Lorentz, with the exception that we have to calculate p in the right way.
assets.caption_hint: Recovery of the three-dimensional Lorentz force

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: Shows the transverse transformation in which an electric component acquires a magnetic contribution.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The second component of the electric field mixes in with a little bit of the third component of the magnetic field.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_14.png
assets.rationale: Shows the invariant scalar wave operator and its time-minus-space component expansion.
